from.place: Proof, “The integral twist”: finite coefficients (O_E/ell^m)_X in the inverse system; coefficient-field transition through their integral reductions, used by the rational/algebraic-closure paragraph.

title: The induced quotient inclusion is characterized by the two integral reductions.
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\subseteq F\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the restricted absolute values and integer rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_F$ of [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring], and let $X$ be any scheme. For $G=E,F$ and $n\geq0$, put $B_{G,n}=\mathcal O_G/\ell^{n+1}\mathcal O_G$, with the discrete topology, and let $q_{G,n}:\mathcal O_G\to B_{G,n}$ be reduction, a continuous ring homomorphism ([lem-sp-ell-quotient-finite-discrete]), with condensation $\underline{q_{G,n}}$ of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Write $\underline T(S)=C(S,T)$ for the underlying abelian sheaf of the condensed ring of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $T_X=p_X^*\underline T$ using [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Let $r_{G,n}=p_X^*\underline{q_{G,n}}:\mathcal O_{G,X}\to B_{G,n,X}$ be the coefficient map of [def-sfb-coefficient-map]. Let $\iota_{E,F}:\underline E\to\underline F$ be the field inclusion of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map] and $\kappa_G:\underline{\mathcal O}_G\to\underline G$ the integer inclusion of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point]. Let $i_{E,F,X}:\mathcal O_{E,X}\to\mathcal O_{F,X}$ be the unique morphism of ring objects with $(\kappa_F)_X\circ i_{E,F,X}=(\iota_{E,F})_X\circ(\kappa_E)_X$, given by [lem-route-sp-integers-map-exists-unique]. Then there exists exactly one morphism of abelian sheaves
$$\phi:B_{E,n,X}\longrightarrow B_{F,n,X}$$
satisfying
$$\phi\circ r_{E,n}=r_{F,n}\circ i_{E,F,X}.$$
The uniqueness is among all abelian-sheaf morphisms, without requiring them to preserve the ring structures.

proof.text: The inclusions into the fixed algebraic closure identify the restricted norms on $E$ and $F$, so $j:\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$, $x\mapsto x$, is a continuous unital ring homomorphism: membership is $|x|\leq1$, and both topologies are subspace topologies. By [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] and [def-sfb-coefficient-map], $p_X^*\underline j$ is a ring-object morphism. Its composite with $\mathcal O_{F,X}\to F_X$ equals the composite $\mathcal O_{E,X}\to E_X\to F_X$: before pullback both send $a:S\to\mathcal O_E$ to the same function $S\to F$, and functors preserve composition. The two field and integer inclusion maps here are those of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map] and [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point]. The uniqueness clause of [lem-route-sp-integers-map-exists-unique] therefore identifies $p_X^*\underline j=i_{E,F,X}$.

source.place: Field-extension transitions: identify the selected integral map with pullback of the actual continuous integer inclusion

proof.text: Define $\bar j:B_{E,n}\to B_{F,n}$ by $[x]\mapsto[j(x)]$. This is well-defined: if $x-y=\ell^{n+1}a$ in $\mathcal O_E$, then $j(x)-j(y)=\ell^{n+1}j(a)$ in $\mathcal O_F$. Addition, multiplication and one are preserved by applying $j$ to representatives. Thus $\bar j q_{E,n}=q_{F,n}j$. The discrete quotient topologies make $\bar j$ continuous. For $G=E,F$ the absolute value $|x|_G=|x|$ restricted from $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ ([def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring]) restricts to $|\cdot|_\ell$ on $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq G$, so by the uniqueness in clause 1 of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] it is the extending absolute value there; hence $\mathcal O_G=\{|x|_G\le1\}$ of [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring] is the ring of clause 2, with the topology of [def-sfb-coefficient-extension-integers-topology]. So [lem-sp-ell-quotient-finite-discrete] applies to $E$ and $F$ with exponent $n+1$: the reductions are continuous and the quotients finite.

source.place: Integral finite quotient coefficients: descend the actual inclusion modulo the same positive power of ell

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] to $\bar j,q_{E,n},q_{F,n},j$. On a profinite test $S$, the two composites in their square send $a:S\to\mathcal O_E$ to $s\mapsto[j(a(s))]$, so they agree. Apply the functor $p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] and use the coefficient-map definition [def-sfb-coefficient-map]. The resulting morphism $\phi=p_X^*\underline{\bar j}$ satisfies $\phi r_{E,n}=r_{F,n}i_{E,F,X}$ by step 1. It is in particular a morphism of the underlying abelian sheaves, giving existence.

source.place: Field-extension transitions: condense the quotient map and pull its commuting reduction square back to X

proof.text: Put $q=\underline{q_{E,n}}$. For any profinite $S$ and $b\in C(S,B_{E,n})$, choose for each of the finitely many $t\in B_{E,n}$ a representative $a_t\in\mathcal O_E$. Then $a(s)=a_{b(s)}$ is continuous: each fibre $b^{-1}(t)$ is open, and the inverse image of any open subset of $\mathcal O_E$ under $a$ is a union of these fibres. Moreover $q_{E,n}a=b$. Hence every component $q(S)$ is surjective. If additive sheaf maps $u,v$ out of $\underline{B_{E,n}}$ agree after $q$, evaluation on such lifts gives $u_S(b)=v_S(b)$ for every $S,b$; thus $u=v$. This proves that $q$ is epimorphic directly, using precisely the finiteness from [lem-sp-ell-quotient-finite-discrete] (applicable by step 2) and the section description of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring].

source.place: Uniqueness: a section of the finite discrete quotient lifts by choosing representatives of its finitely many values

proof.text: Use the adjunction $p_X^*\dashv p_{X*}$ stated in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. For any abelian sheaf $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, transpose maps $u,v:p_X^*\underline{B_{E,n}}\to H$ to $u^\#,v^\#:\underline{B_{E,n}}\to p_{X*}H$. Naturality of this Hom bijection in its source sends $u\circ p_X^*q=v\circ p_X^*q$ to $u^\#q=v^\#q$. Step 4 gives $u^\#=v^\#$; the bijection then gives $u=v$. Thus $r_{E,n}=p_X^*q$ is epimorphic. Apply this cancellation to any two morphisms satisfying the asserted square: their composites with $r_{E,n}$ both equal $r_{F,n}i_{E,F,X}$, hence they coincide. This proves uniqueness in the full abelian-sheaf Hom set.

source.place: Uniqueness: transport cancellation through the point-pullback adjunction, then cancel the pulled-back reduction
